# Overview

This page describes the
**beta-binomial** extension, which models the extra cell-line-to-cell-line
variance directly rather than assuming pure binomial sampling noise.

Sites tested: the same **5-fold union (≥ 1 fold)** set,
**`r format(12416, big.mark=",")` sites**. Samples: the same **50 genotyped
cell lines**. Covariates: the same **M-value PCs** (below).

# The model

For a given pU site, let individual $i$ have $y_i$ converted reads out of
$n_i$ total reads, but now allow the modification rate itself to vary around
its mean $\mu_i$ (a Beta-distributed mixing probability):

$$
p_i \sim \text{Beta}(\alpha_i, \beta_i), \qquad y_i \mid p_i \sim \text{Binomial}(n_i, p_i)
$$
$$
\text{logit}(\mu_i) = \beta_0 + \beta_g G_i + z_i^\top\gamma, \qquad
\mu_i = \frac{\alpha_i}{\alpha_i+\beta_i}, \qquad
\phi = \frac{1}{\alpha_i+\beta_i+1}
$$

Marginalizing over $p_i$ gives the **beta-binomial** distribution for $y_i$,
with the same mean model as the binomial but a different variance:

$$
\text{Var}(y_i) = n_i\mu_i(1-\mu_i)\big[\,1+(n_i-1)\phi\,\big]
$$

- $\phi \in [0,1)$ — the **overdispersion / intra-class-correlation**
  parameter: how much the $n_i$ reads at one cell line behave like correlated
  (not independent) trials. $\phi=0$ recovers the binomial exactly.
- The bracketed term $1+(n_i-1)\phi$ is a **variance inflation factor** — the
  same form as the design effect in clustered/survey data. It grows with
  depth $n_i$, so high-depth cell lines are *not* automatically down-weighted
  as much as the binomial would assume, once $\phi>0$.
- One $\phi$ per site (not per cell line, not per SNP) — a single dispersion
  shared across the site's 50 observations.

# QTL mapping: the beta-binomial LRT

Per (site, cis-SNP) pair, $\beta_g$ is tested with a **likelihood-ratio
test**: fit the full model (with the cis-SNP) and the covariates-only null
model by maximum likelihood ($\beta_0,\gamma,\phi$ jointly for each), compare
log-likelihoods:

$$
\Lambda = 2\big(\log\text{Lik}_{\text{full}} - \log\text{Lik}_{\text{null}}\big)
\;\overset{H_0}{\sim}\; \chi^2_1, \qquad H_0:\ \beta_g = 0
$$

```r
nf_null <- fit_bb_mle(y, n, X)         # joint MLE: beta0, gamma, phi
nf_full <- fit_bb_mle(y, n, cbind(X, g))
stat <- max(2 * (nf_full$loglik - nf_null$loglik), 0)
p_snp <- pchisq(stat, df = 1, lower.tail = FALSE)
```

**Why the LRT, matching the binomial model's decision.** A faster **Rao
score test** (fit the null once per site, test every cis-SNP via a
vectorized computation, using the exact digamma/trigamma score and
information of the beta-binomial log-likelihood — closed form via
$k=(1-\phi)/\phi$, $a_i=\mu_ik$, $b_i=(1-\mu_i)k$) was built and validated
first, since a full-model refit per cis-SNP is far more expensive than one
null fit per site. It performs *better* here than the binomial's score test
did — validated against a numerical gradient/Hessian (exact match) and
against the real LRT (rank correlation **0.955** on real sites, essentially
unbiased) — but the underlying concern is the same structural one that
motivated the binomial's switch: the score test's variance is a subtraction
of two similarly-sized quantities ($V = G^\top\text{diag}(w)G - (\cdots)$),
which is exposed to cancellation and near-singularity failure modes that a
directly-computed log-likelihood comparison isn't. 0.955 is good, not
perfect, and for consistency with the binomial's LRT-based final results the
same test is used here.

**Making the LRT affordable.** A full-model refit per cis-SNP per
permutation was originally estimated at ~200,000+ CPU-hours for a full
24-config scan — infeasible. Two optimizations to `fit_bb_mle()` (2026-07-27)
brought this down substantially: (1) dropping the constant `lchoose(n,y)`
term from the per-iteration objective (it cancels exactly in the LRT
statistic anyway) and (2) supplying the optimizer an **analytic gradient**
(reusing the same digamma-based score derivation as the exact score test
above) instead of finite-difference — together roughly a **2.5-2.9x**
speedup, validated against the original implementation's fitted values on
real sites (matching to 1e-4) before being adopted. Combined with running a
**preliminary pass at 100 permutations** (not the full 1000) to rank
PC/window configs and check calibration — verified via Monte Carlo to stay
unbiased with about twice the noise of 500 permutations, adequate for this
purpose — the full 24-config grid now costs **~3,000 CPU-hours** total.
Permutations will be increased once the best config is chosen.

Note the LRT's permutation loop no longer needs the fixed-$\phi$
mean-only-refit shortcut described in the score-test era below — with the
optimizer this fast, every permutation just refits the full joint MLE
directly.

# Significance

Same three-step procedure as the binomial model.

## 1. Permutation as a calibration check

Same audit as the binomial: permute the phenotype and covariates together
across the 50 cell lines (5 seeds; genotype stays fixed), refit **fresh**
(phi re-estimated under each permutation), collect nominal LRT p-values,
check $\lambda\approx1$.

## 2. Within-site correction (permutation beta-approximation)

Same procedure as the binomial: minimum nominal p across a site's cis-SNPs,
permutation null of that minimum, Beta(a,b) fit, adjusted per-site p from
the Beta CDF.

## 3. Across-site correction

BH-FDR (and q-values) over the per-site adjusted p, same as the binomial.

# Model fit across PC counts

The joint MLE ($k$ PCs + intercept + $\phi$) is reliably fittable across the
full swept range, $k\in\3,5,7,10,15,20\}$: ~7,600 of 12,416 sites fit at k=20 (vs.
the binomial's ~7,900 at the same k). See the [results
page](qtl_mapping_summary_betabinomial.html) for the sites-fit table.

# Data

- **Sites**: 5-fold union, ≥ 1 fold — `r format(12416, big.mark=",")` pU sites.
- **Phenotype**: per site, per cell line — converted reads $C$ ($=y$) out of
  total depth $N$ ($=C+T$), identical to the binomial model (no
  transformation).
- **Genotypes**: cis SNPs within a window of each site (±5/20/50/100kb),
  common variants (MAF≥0.05) from the 50 cell lines' genotypes.
- **Covariates $z$**: M-value phenotype PCs — identical construction to the
  [binomial model](qtl_mapping_binomial_model.html#Covariates:_M-value_phenotype_PCs)
  (site-specific $(\pi_s, 1-\pi_s)$ pseudocount), swept over
  $k \in \{3,5,7,10,15,20\}$ (reliably fittable across the full range).
